- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually increase — suggesting a lag in capturing short-term momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 78–85 range), model overreacts with exaggerated upward forecasts, then corrects too late.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to anticipate price pullback after peaks, often holding high forecasts too long.
- Forecasts for the last 5–10 days of the 30-day window are often too high, suggesting overconfidence in near-term continuation.
- Model underestimates volatility in the middle of the forecast horizon — misses downward corrections after initial upticks.
- When history includes recent high prices, model tends to forecast lower than true outcome, indicating failure to recognize momentum continuation.
- Model exhibits bias toward smoothing out volatility — underestimates sharp drops and overestimates gradual declines.
